name: Andritz AG
executive_summary:
Andritz AG is a global capital-equipment and engineering group (pulp & paper, metals, hydropower, separation) listed on the Vienna Stock Exchange. The quantitative screen rates it a **Strong Buy**, driven by a 7.3% FCF yield, 20.2% ROE, 3.4% dividend yield, and passes across cheapness, quality, dividend, GARP, and risk families (9/22 models). The valuation hook is a quality industrial compounder trading at ~17× earnings and ~3.3× book, with Neff PEGY of 0.05 on ~6.7% earnings growth. The central debate is whether record order backlog (EUR 12.9bn per Q2 2026 news) and margin expansion offset a visible FY2025 revenue and earnings step-down—and whether the screen’s quality signal survives a cyclical downturn in capex-heavy end markets. Primary regulatory filings were not retrieved; this memo should be treated as verify-before-trade.

---
investment_thesis:
For a value investor, Andritz offers a rare combination of **cash generation, balance-sheet resilience, and shareholder return** at a mid-teens multiple—not deep Graham territory (P/B 3.3 fails net-net and Schloss screens), but compelling on cash-adjusted metrics.

**Quantitative alignment:** The screen passes FCF Yield, Neff PEGY (0.05), Quality Value, Buffett Quality, Dividend Growth, Magic Formula, Composite Value, Earnings Quality, and Financial Health. Debt/equity of ~25% (screen input), positive operating cash flow, declining leverage (Piotroski), and no share dilution support the risk-family pass. FCF yield of 7.3% on canonical TTM FCF of ~USD 575m (screen) versus a 3.4% dividend yield implies meaningful retained cash for reinvestment or debt reduction.

**Business quality:** Andritz operates in oligopolistic process-industry niches with long project cycles and high aftermarket/service content—news flow cites service at ~46% of revenue (Q1 2026) and a record EUR 12.9bn backlog (Q2 2026), which supports revenue visibility and margin stability through cycles. ROE of 20.2% and gross margins above 50% (Yahoo FY2025: EUR 4.03bn gross profit on EUR 7.88bn revenue) indicate pricing power and engineering moats, even though the Economic Moat model fails on ROA (<8%) and margin thresholds.

**Why Strong Buy, not merely Hold:** The screen’s GARP and quality-value passes suggest the market may be penalising FY2025 revenue decline (EUR 7.88bn vs EUR 8.31bn in 2024) while underpricing forward earnings power from backlog conversion and margin corridor progress (three of four business areas within 2027 targets per Q2 2026 earnings coverage). For value investors who accept moderate P/B in exchange for FCF yield and dividend growth, the risk/reward skews favourable—provided cyclical and pension risks are sized appropriately.

financial_review:
**Primary filing gap:** `filings_index.json` (regime: `euro_filings`) lists **zero** annual reports, interim results, or trading updates, with no body extracts under `filings/bodies/`. Interim and annual analysis below therefore relies entirely on **Yahoo fallback** (`financials_annual.json`) and news headlines; figures should be reconciled to Andritz’s official Geschäftsbericht and half-year reports before trading.

### Annual trends (Yahoo FY2022–FY2025, EUR)

| Metric | FY2022 | FY2023 | FY2024 | FY2025 |
|--------|--------|--------|--------|--------|
| Revenue | 7.54bn | 8.66bn | 8.31bn | 7.88bn |
| Operating income | 540m | 666m | 649m | 586m |
| EBITDA | 826m | 962m | 923m | 889m |
| Net income | 410m | 510m | 497m | 456m |
| Diluted EPS | 4.13 | 5.13 | 4.99 | 4.65 |
| Operating CF | 711m | 375m | 637m | 653m |
| Free cash flow | 556m | 204m | 457m | 455m |
| Dividends paid | 164m | 208m | 249m | 254m |

**Revenue and earnings:** Revenue peaked in FY2023 and has declined for two consecutive years (−5.2% in FY2024, −5.2% in FY2025). Net income followed, down 8.3% in FY2025 vs FY2024, though still well above FY2022 levels. Restructuring and M&A charges appear in each year (e.g. EUR 44m restructuring/M&A in FY2025 per Yahoo), partially explaining volatility.

**Profitability:** Gross margin held above 51% in FY2025; operating margin compressed to ~7.4% (586m/7.88bn) from ~7.8% in FY2024. EBITDA margin ~11.3% in FY2025 vs ~11.1% in FY2024—modest resilience despite lower volume.

**Cash flow:** FY2023 FCF was weak (EUR 204m) on heavy working-capital absorption (EUR −446m WC change); FY2024–FY2025 normalised to ~EUR 455–457m. TTM FCF per Yahoo quarterly roll-forward: ~EUR 468m. Capex FY2025: EUR 198m. FY2025 included EUR 329m business acquisitions (cash investing), lifting goodwill from EUR 860m (FY2024) to EUR 1.13bn (FY2025)—integration risk worth monitoring.

**Balance sheet (Yahoo FY2025, EUR):** Total assets EUR 8.61bn; equity EUR 2.46bn; total debt EUR 831m (long-term debt EUR 364m + leases). Cash EUR 912m; net debt modest. Working capital EUR 626m (down from EUR 794m FY2024). **Current ratio 1.13** (screen)—below Graham’s 2.0 threshold and flagged in model failures. **Pension:** non-current pension/post-retirement EUR 315m plus current pension EUR 387m (~EUR 701m combined)—material off-balance-sheet-style obligation.

**Shareholder returns:** Dividends rose steadily (EUR 254m FY2025; ~56% payout on net income). Share count stable (~98m diluted); treasury shares ~6.0m. Buybacks minimal in FY2025 (none per cash flow); EUR 117m repurchased in FY2024.

|--------|---------|------------|-------------|

Q2 2026 revenue and reported net income are lower YoY on Yahoo data. **News context (not blended into Yahoo numbers):** Q2 2026 earnings coverage (1 Aug 2026, Yahoo Finance) cites a **15% jump in comparable EBITDA** and **record EUR 12.9bn order backlog**, with shares rising ~6–7% (Investing.com, 30 Jul 2026). Q1 2026 coverage (30 Apr 2026) reported backlog of EUR 12.4bn and service at 46% of revenue. The divergence between softer reported quarterly net income (Yahoo) and stronger adjusted/backlog narrative in news warrants reconciliation to official half-year filings.

**Screen vs Yahoo FCF:** Screen canonical FCF ~USD 575m (TTM) vs Yahoo FY2025 FCF EUR 455m and TTM EUR 468m—directionally consistent; currency and timing may explain the gap.

risks_and_flags:
**Cyclical exposure:** Capital equipment demand in pulp & paper, metals, and hydropower is project-lumpy and capex-cycle sensitive. FY2025 revenue decline (−5%) may reflect end-market softness; backlog provides visibility but does not eliminate cancellation or deferral risk.

**Earnings quality / trend:** Two-year revenue decline and FY2025 net income down 8% contradict the screen’s growth input (6.7%). Piotroski F-Score 6/9—fails on ROA improvement, current-ratio improvement, and asset turnover improvement. Lynch PEG 2.54 fails (>1.0).

**Balance sheet / liquidity:** Current ratio 1.13 is tight for a project business with EUR 1.21bn inventory and EUR 1.29bn receivables (FY2025 Yahoo). No filing-body language on covenants, going concern, or contingencies was available to review.

**Pension:** Combined pension provisions ~EUR 701m (FY2025 Yahoo)—meaningful relative to equity of EUR 2.46bn; sensitivity to discount rates and longevity not assessable without annual report notes.

**M&A / goodwill:** EUR 329m acquisitions in FY2025; goodwill +intangibles EUR 1.38bn (~16% of assets). Impairment risk if integration underperforms.

**Competitive:** Peer set includes Valmet and Metso; Andritz stock rose on Valmet’s strong results (Investing.com, 24 Jul 2026), indicating correlated sector read-through.

**Governance / disclosure:** No primary filings retrieved; unable to assess related-party transactions, auditor emphasis, or management guidance from regulatory sources.

**Regulatory:** No material regulatory actions surfaced in the news manifest; coverage is thin on compliance topics.

RiskTags: cyclical, pension, competitive, leverage, liquidity, accounting, other

research_rationale: The quantitative Strong Buy is directionally supported by FCF yield, ROE, dividend profile, and news of record backlog with improving comparable margins, but the absence of primary filings and visible FY2025 revenue/earnings decline prevent full confirmation of the screen signal.
